item: Pool and disk: the route that holds a connection, a poll that never waits on the pool, a plain disk I/O error read against free space
key_paths: src/database/pool_watch.py; src/scheduler/plan_cache.py; src/api/insights.py; src/api/scheduler.py; src/api/main.py; src/monitoring/stall_forensics.py; src/scheduler/storage_guard.py; src/versioned/store.py; src/database/session.py; src/scheduler/runner.py; src/config/memory_budget.py; src/static/app-core.js; src/static/taskmanager.js
summary: Diagnostics ranks 7 and 12 and the disk gap. Every pooled connection is listed with the route that took it (a ContextVar the request middleware sets, copied into anyio's worker thread), the last twenty pool invalidations are kept with the DBAPI's own message and never a statement, and the stall record files the pool as it stands (the oldest eight holders by thread, route and age, the count of all, the reservation's counts; evidence only, an unreadable instrument is a stated gap). The status probe no longer holds one pooled slot for the process's life (detached, closed when its engine is disposed) and the pass summary's headroom subtracts the non-collector checkouts older than a minute. GET /api/scheduler/activity no longer opens a session: the next-pass preview is served from the last good computation, labelled with its age, refreshed by at most one background thread, and never shown for settings the operator has since changed (three strings in 12 locales, both UIs). SQLite's plain disk I/O error latches the storage guard only when the drive's free space read at that moment is below the reserve (the same message is a dying drive's, so the message alone never latches), on the corpus engine and now on every lane engine; with room, or unreadable, it is recorded (io_errors, last_io_error) and left to the drive watchdog. The guard measures the tail between its first refusal and the end of the pass in flight (numbers only; the drive figure is an upper bound). Also folds in the Opus read of #1287: the drain stamps its end however it ended, the supervisor's stop check and its thread's publication are one step under the stop lock, the pool-timeout test no longer hard-codes the Linux limit, two shipped-row sentences corrected.
